newsitem.title: UK: Singapore refiners make $5/bbl but West closes gap.
newsitem.headline: Singapore refiners make $5/bbl but West closes gap.

text.p: Profit margins at Singapore refineries remain much higher than their Western competitors but the gap is slowly narrowing, according to Reuter price data using standard product yields.
A complex refinery in Singapore makes $5.07 a barrel refining Dubai crude while a similar plant in Rotterdam processing Brent blend makes just $1.81.
But the gap in profitability has narrowed this month from nearly $4 a barrel in the first week of March to $3.26 last Friday.
In Singapore over the past couple of weeks the value of gasoline has fallen over $2.50 a barrel against Dubai crude but gas oil and fuel have only slipped slightly.
Gas oil made big gains during February and the first half of March but slipped off its $9.80 a barrel peak last week.
In the West refinery profitability continued to edge higher from the lows hit in February but they remain depressed.
In Rotterdam complex plants running Brent ended last week at $1.43 a barrel compared to profits of just 95 cents in the first week of March.
But hydroskimming plants were still running at a loss as they have since since mid-February with only breif repreive.
Dealers said the persistent weakness on wet Brent and modest gains on gasoline remain the driving forces behind better profits.
Other oil products such as heavy fuel and winter heating oil were doing little to help profits.
Mediterranean profit margins gained ground last week and hydroskimming plants made a profit running Urals for the first time since Janaury.
The refinery maintenance season in the Mediterranean and continuing exports of Iraqi crude oil help keep Urals prices under pressure.
In the U.S. Gulf, refiners ended last week making profits of $1.81 a barrel running Brent and 59 cents a barrel on West Texas Intermediate.
This compares with 48 cents and zero cents respectively in the first week of March.
